_comment: Sea animals (scripts/sim/sea_life.gd), just for looking at: they never affect ships. Kinds: whale, orca and dolphin (the pods), fish (schools: salmon, tuna, marlin, sailfish, swordfish, mahi-mahi, wahoo, tarpon, trevally, barracuda, kingfish, mackerel, bass, halibut, cod), shark, seal, sea_lion and otter. breach is a leap for dolphins, fish and sea lions and a breach for whales, orcas and sharks; surface shows the animal at the top (with a blow for whales and orcas only: sharks show their fin, seals and sea lions bob up, otters float on their backs). Each pod spends parts of the year in areas (stays: [area, from MM-DD, to MM-DD], by the in-game calendar), wandering about each, and migrates between them along a sea path the game finds (around land) in the gaps. Positions follow from the calendar alone, so every player sees the same pods and nothing is saved. size is the pod's real number of animals; the map draws at most the species' shown of them. Species: length_px is how long one is drawn (before growing zoomed in), spacing_px how far apart a pod's animals swim, surface (whales and orcas) how often [every s of play, chance] one comes up to breathe and blow, breach how often [every s, chance] one breaches (dolphins: leaps), length_m and fact for its popup. Pod sizes follow the real ones: bottlenose dolphins 2-15 near the coast, spinner dolphins 50-200, orcas 3-5 (transients) to 10-20 (residents), sperm whale family units 10-15 (young males in small groups), and the great whales alone or in twos and threes.

bottlenose.name: Bottlenose dolphin
bottlenose.fact: They call each other by name: each has its own signature whistle.

spinner.name: Spinner dolphin
spinner.fact: Famous for leaping clear of the water and spinning up to seven times before splashing down.

orca.name: Orca
orca.fact: Killer whales are really the biggest dolphins; each pod has its own dialect of calls.

humpback.name: Humpback whale
humpback.fact: Their long white flippers are a third of their length, and the males sing songs that can last 20 minutes.

blue.name: Blue whale
blue.fact: The largest animal that has ever lived; its heart is the size of a small car.

gray.name: Gray whale
gray.fact: Every year they swim about 10,000 miles there and back, one of the longest migrations of any mammal.

sperm.name: Sperm whale
sperm.fact: They dive over a mile deep after squid, and have the biggest brain of any animal.

right.name: Southern right whale
right.fact: The white bumps on their heads are callosities, a pattern as unique as a fingerprint.

fin.name: Fin whale
fin.fact: The second-biggest animal on Earth and one of the fastest whales: the greyhound of the sea sprints at 25 knots. Only its right jaw is white.

beluga.name: Beluga whale
beluga.fact: The canary of the sea chirps, whistles and clicks, and unlike other whales it can turn its head to look about.

narwhal.name: Narwhal
narwhal.fact: The male's spiral tusk is a tooth up to 3 m long, grown out through its upper lip and packed with nerve endings.

common_dolphin.name: Common dolphin
common_dolphin.fact: Superpods thousands strong churn the sea white as they herd sardines into bait balls; the golden hourglass on each side gives them away.

dusky.name: Dusky dolphin
dusky.fact: Among the most acrobatic of all dolphins, flipping head over tail again and again in the air.

spotted.name: Atlantic spotted dolphin
spotted.fact: Calves are born without spots and grow spottier every year.

chinook_salmon.name: Chinook salmon
chinook_salmon.fact: The king salmon: the biggest of the Pacific salmon, running up the Columbia and the Yukon to spawn where they hatched.

sockeye_salmon.name: Sockeye salmon
sockeye_salmon.fact: Silver at sea, they turn scarlet with green heads on the way up to their spawning lakes; tens of millions run into Bristol Bay each summer.

coho_salmon.name: Coho salmon
coho_salmon.fact: The silver salmon, a favourite of anglers for the way it leaps and runs when hooked.

pink_salmon.name: Pink salmon
pink_salmon.fact: The smallest and most numerous Pacific salmon; the spawning males grow a hump, so they're called humpies.

chum_salmon.name: Chum salmon
chum_salmon.fact: Dog salmon, for the big teeth the spawning males grow; they range further than any other salmon, from California to Korea and the Arctic.

atlantic_salmon.name: Atlantic salmon
atlantic_salmon.fact: Unlike the Pacific salmon it can spawn more than once, going back to sea between runs; it feeds off Greenland and the Faroes.

bluefin_tuna.name: Atlantic bluefin tuna
bluefin_tuna.fact: Warm-blooded and built for speed, a giant bluefin can weigh over 600 kg and cross the Atlantic in under two months.

yellowfin_tuna.name: Yellowfin tuna
yellowfin_tuna.fact: Its long sickle fins turn bright yellow with age; schools often swim beneath dolphins in the eastern Pacific.

albacore.name: Albacore
albacore.fact: The white-meat tuna, with pectoral fins half as long as its body; it sweeps across the North Pacific every summer.

skipjack.name: Skipjack tuna
skipjack.fact: The most caught fish in the world, in schools of thousands that boil at the surface chasing bait.

blue_marlin.name: Blue marlin
blue_marlin.fact: The grander, a marlin over 1,000 pounds, is the dream of big-game anglers; the females are many times the size of the males.

black_marlin.name: Black marlin
black_marlin.fact: Its pectoral fins are fixed and can't fold flat; off Cairns in spring the biggest black marlin in the world gather to spawn.

striped_marlin.name: Striped marlin
striped_marlin.fact: The most acrobatic of the marlin, lighting up its blue stripes as it hunts; off Cabo they herd baitballs together.

sailfish.name: Sailfish
sailfish.fact: The fastest fish in the sea, clocked near 110 km/h; it raises its huge sail to herd sardines into a ball.

swordfish.name: Swordfish
swordfish.fact: It hunts squid 600 m down by day, warming its eyes and brain with special muscles, and rises to the surface at night.

mahi_mahi.name: Mahi-mahi
mahi_mahi.fact: The dolphinfish, or dorado: blazing gold, green and blue, it grows faster than almost any fish and gathers under floating weed and logs.

wahoo.name: Wahoo
wahoo.fact: A great barred mackerel that strikes at 75 km/h, screaming line off the reel; sailors named it for the shout it earns.

tarpon.name: Tarpon
tarpon.fact: The silver king: armoured in huge scales, it gulps air at the surface and leaps and crashes when hooked, throwing most hooks.

giant_trevally.name: Giant trevally
giant_trevally.fact: The GT: a brutal reef predator that has been filmed leaping clear of the water to snatch seabirds from the air.

barracuda.name: Great barracuda
barracuda.fact: A hanging torpedo of teeth that follows swimmers out of curiosity; it strikes at anything that flashes like a fish.

yellowtail.name: Yellowtail kingfish
yellowtail.fact: The hoodlum of the reef edge: schools of kingfish hit lures in a pack and dive straight for the rocks to cut the line.

king_mackerel.name: King mackerel
king_mackerel.fact: The kingfish of the Gulf and Carolina coasts, famous for skyrocketing: a kingfish leaps high clear of the water to hit a bait from below.

striped_bass.name: Striped bass
striped_bass.fact: The striper runs up the Chesapeake's rivers to spawn each spring and summers off New England, where surfcasters wait for the blitzes.

halibut.name: Pacific halibut
halibut.fact: A barn door: a big halibut lies flat on the bottom, both eyes on its brown side, and can weigh over 200 kg.

atlantic_cod.name: Atlantic cod
atlantic_cod.fact: The fish that drew the fleets of Europe to the Grand Banks for 500 years; the skrei run in to Lofoten every winter to spawn.

great_white.name: Great white shark
great_white.fact: Off Guadalupe and the Farallones they feed on seals in autumn, then swim out to the White Shark Cafe in mid-ocean every spring.

tiger_shark.name: Tiger shark
tiger_shark.fact: The dustbin of the sea: tiger sharks have been found with licence plates, tyres and a suit of armour inside them.

hammerhead.name: Scalloped hammerhead
hammerhead.fact: They school by the hundred round seamounts like Cocos and the Galapagos by day, and scatter to hunt alone at night.

mako.name: Shortfin mako
mako.fact: The fastest shark, warm-blooded like the tuna it chases, and the only one that leaps six metres clear of the water.

bull_shark.name: Bull shark
bull_shark.fact: The only big shark at home in fresh water: bull sharks have been caught 4,000 km up the Amazon and in the Mississippi at Illinois.

whale_shark.name: Whale shark
whale_shark.fact: The biggest fish in the sea, a gentle filter feeder; every whale shark's pattern of spots is its own, like a fingerprint.

harbor_seal.name: Harbour seal
harbor_seal.fact: The common seal of both coasts of the North Atlantic and Pacific, hauled out on sandbars at low tide in a banana pose, head and tail up.

grey_seal.name: Grey seal
grey_seal.fact: Horse-headed and big; half the world's grey seals pup on Sable Island, a sandbar out in the Atlantic off Nova Scotia.

elephant_seal.name: Northern elephant seal
elephant_seal.fact: Bulls of over two tonnes roar through their trunks on the beaches each winter; at sea they dive to 1,500 m and stay down an hour.

leopard_seal.name: Leopard seal
leopard_seal.fact: The Antarctic's hunter of penguins, with a reptile's grin; it sings under the ice in the breeding season.

california_sea_lion.name: California sea lion
california_sea_lion.fact: The barking seal of the piers: it porpoises through the swell, steers with its long foreflippers and can walk on all fours ashore.

steller_sea_lion.name: Steller sea lion
steller_sea_lion.fact: The biggest sea lion, a tawny bull of a tonne roaring over its rookery on the Aleutian rocks.

australian_sea_lion.name: Australian sea lion
australian_sea_lion.fact: Found only on the south and west coasts of Australia; the bulls' chocolate coats go cream on the head and neck.

sea_otter.name: Sea otter
sea_otter.fact: It floats on its back cracking clams on a stone it keeps in a pocket of skin, wrapped in kelp so it doesn't drift off while it sleeps.

marine_otter.name: Marine otter
marine_otter.fact: The chungungo, the smallest sea mammal, hunting crabs along the wave-washed rocks of Chile and Peru.

atlantic_herring.name: Atlantic herring
atlantic_herring.fact: Shoals of herring a few kilometres long fed the Hanseatic League; they spawn in their billions on the gravel banks of the North Sea and off Norway.

sardine.name: Sardine
sardine.fact: Pilchards in the Atlantic, sardines in the Mediterranean: Portugal and Galicia grill them by the million each summer.

anchovy.name: European anchovy
anchovy.fact: Salted in Collioure and Cantabria since the Romans; the Bay of Biscay's spring fishery runs from April to June.

anchoveta.name: Peruvian anchoveta
anchoveta.fact: The world's biggest fishery by weight: up to 10 million tonnes a year off Peru, most of it ground into fishmeal.

capelin.name: Capelin
capelin.fact: A small smelt the cod, seals and whales of the North Atlantic live on; it rolls up the beaches of Newfoundland to spawn each June.

menhaden.name: Atlantic menhaden
menhaden.fact: 'The most important fish in the sea': too bony to eat, it's caught by the hundred thousand tonnes for oil and bait in Chesapeake Bay and the Gulf.

sprat.name: European sprat
sprat.fact: The Baltic's most-caught fish: smoked in Riga as brisling, tinned in Norway.

pacific_saury.name: Pacific saury
pacific_saury.fact: Sanma, the taste of autumn in Japan: caught at night off Hokkaido with lights that draw the shoals to the boats.

atlantic_mackerel.name: Atlantic mackerel
atlantic_mackerel.fact: Tiger-striped and fast: the North Atlantic's mackerel shoals sweep from Biscay to Norway and Iceland each year.

jack_mackerel.name: Jack mackerel
jack_mackerel.fact: Its shoals once spanned the South Pacific from Chile almost to New Zealand; Chile's purse seiners still land hundreds of thousands of tonnes.

alaska_pollock.name: Alaska pollock
alaska_pollock.fact: The fish in fish sticks and surimi: the Bering Sea's pollock fishery lands over a million tonnes a year.

haddock.name: Haddock
haddock.fact: Known by its black lateral line and the dark 'thumbprint' over its fin: the fish in Britain's fish and chips.

hake.name: Hake
hake.fact: Spain eats more hake than anywhere: from Galician trawlers, and from the Patagonian and Namibian shelves.

churchill.name: the Churchill River mouth, Hudson Bay

central_america.name: the Pacific coast of Costa Rica and Panama

ecuador_colombia.name: the Pacific coast of Colombia and Ecuador

madeira_canaries.name: the seas between Madeira and the Canaries

southern_ocean_africa.name: the Southern Ocean south of Africa

head_of_bight.name: the Head of the Great Australian Bight

southern_ocean_aus.name: the Southern Ocean south of Australia

east_antarctic.name: the Antarctic waters south of Australia

kaikoura.name: the waters off Kaikoura, New Zealand

strait_of_georgia.name: the west coast of Vancouver Island

cairns.name: the Great Barrier Reef off Cairns

cabo.name: the waters off Cabo San Lucas

costa_rica_pacific.name: the Pacific coast of Costa Rica

juan_de_fuca.name: the mouth of the Strait of Juan de Fuca

prince_william_sound.name: the mouth of Prince William Sound

pods.name: Great Australian Bight southern right whales
